## Update to FCC's TCPA Consent Revocation Rules


On September 30, 2026, the Federal Communications Commission (FCC)[adopted new rules and proposed additional changes](https://docs.fcc.gov/public/attachments/FCC-26-67A1.pdf) to revise its Telephone Consumer Protection Act (TCPA) consent revocation rules. The new rules replace the previously planned "revoke all" requirement and officially take effect on November 25, 2026. This update provides key modifications to how callers and text senders handle opt-out requests, allowing for category-specific revocations and designated exclusive opt-out channels.


As always, businesses should consult their own legal counsel to review the specifics of the FCC rules and determine how these regulatory changes apply to their specific messaging architecture and compliance obligations. Twilio is providing this update for informational purposes only.


# What's changing now?


The updated rules modernize several core elements of TCPA compliance:


1. **Category-Specific Revocation:** For informational robocalls and texts (e.g., appointment reminders, billing updates, two factor authentications, etc.) callers may now interpret an opt-out request as applying *only* to that specific category of message rather than revoking consent across all communication types from that sender. Marketing and telemarketing revocations, however, continue to apply to all advertising communications from that sender.
2. **Designation of Exclusive Opt-Out Methods:** Callers may now specify an exclusive, standardized method for consumers to revoke consent rather than being required to process requests made via "any reasonable method.” The FCC approved three exclusive opt-out methods:


1. An automated interactive voice or key press opt-out mechanism during a call;
2. replying to an incoming text message with any one of the following standardized words: “stop,” “quit,” “end,” “revoke,” “optout,” “cancel,” or “unsubscribe”; or
3. a dedicated website or phone number designated by the caller to process opt-outs. ****


**Note:** *Any caller that does not designate one of the methods listed above as the exclusive means to revoke consent must continue to process revocation requests when made in any reasonable manner.*
3. **Expanded Fraud Alert Exemption for Financial Institutions:** Financial institutions sending exempt fraud and identity-theft alerts may now contact wireless numbers obtained from a "reliable source". Reliable sources include numbers provided by an authorized spouse or family member on the account, numbers captured via Caller ID when the customer calls the institution, or records obtained from another financial institution.


# Further Changes Under Review


The FCC is also seeking public comment on additional potential future rule updates and may issue further orders. The proposed changes could include:


- Shortening the maximum timeframe to honor opt-outs from 10 business days to 7 business days;
- Eliminating exceptions for one-way texting protocols to require two-way texting for opt-outs;
- Mandating a single-step "revoke-all" option; and
- Clarifying how revocation rules apply across corporate affiliates, divisions, and separate lines of business.


These proposals may or may not be finalized by the FCC after the public comment period.


# What does this mean for you?


This update provides businesses and communication providers greater certainty when managing TCPA consent compliance while preventing consumers from accidentally opting out of critical, time-sensitive communications (such as security alerts or multi-factor authentication) when the consumer is only seeking to stop certain reminders. Please note, senders and callers must still honor all valid revocation requests within a reasonable time, not to exceed **10 business days** from receipt.


# What should you do?


- **Audit Message Footers:** Verify that your automated SMS messaging workflows include clear and conspicuous disclosures specifying your designated opt-out method (e.g., *"Reply STOP to unsubscribe"* ).
- **Verify Keyword Handlers:** Ensure your messaging platform's application logic continues to recognize all seven standard keywords (` STOP` ,` QUIT` ,` END` ,` REVOKE` ,` OPTOUT` ,` CANCEL` ,` UNSUBSCRIBE` ) even if you only feature one keyword in your footers.
- **Review Customer Preference Workflows:** Align your internal preference databases to handle category-specific revocations for informational messaging programs while maintaining global opt-outs for marketing streams.
- **Designate an Exclusive Method for Opt-out:** Ensure your communication templates clearly and prominently display a single, standardized method for consumers to opt out (such as a specific reply keyword or a dedicated web link), even if your platform is technically capable of processing revocation requests across multiple alternative channels.


*For more information, please visit:*[https://www.twilio.com/docs/messaging/tutorials/advanced-opt-out](https://www.twilio.com/docs/messaging/tutorials/advanced-opt-out)
